transcript:
Meeting header:
- Date/Time: 2026-09-11 15:00 UTC
- Duration: ~41 minutes
- Recording: https://app.fireflies.ai/recordings/ff-20260911-3f9b (note: stub)
- Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Daniel (Redwood SE), Ravi (Redwood CSM); Asha (CTO), Liam (Head of Security), Priya (DevOps), Ellen (Compliance)

Summary:
- PineCoast is evaluating Redwood for an inference layer across hosted, dedicated and private models; primary focus is security posture (SOC2/ISO), SSO/SAML integration, RBAC, audit logs, and encryption/KMS options. They want to understand tradeoffs and what is supported out-of-the-box vs requiring Private deployment.

Topics covered:
- SOC2/ISO certifications and evidence
- SSO/SAML + SCIM provisioning workflow and RBAC mapping
- Audit logs: retention, export, and tamper-evidence
- Encryption: at rest and in transit, BYOK/KMS integration, HSM options
- Data residency and retention policies for logs/models/requests
- Differences between Hosted, Dedicated, and Private deployments for security controls

Transcript (timestamps roughly every 30–60s):
[00:00] Maya Ortega: hey everyone thanks for joining, quick intros then we'll jump into the security points you sent over. uh i'm maya from Redwood AE, daniel's our solutions engineer —
[00:28] Asha Patel: great thanks maya, i'm asha CTO at PineCoast. we run a lot of inference for our telemetry service, main ask is we need to know how we can get SOC2-level assurances and also whether we can bring our own keys.
[00:52] Daniel Cho: yeah hi all, quick note — we'll go through SOC2 artifacts, SSO flow, and then show where logs live in the console. also will call out where dedicated/private change the story.
[01:15] Liam Navarro: to be explicit, we need audit logs retained for at least 1 year, archived in a way that's tamper-evident, and we need to onboard via our SAML provider.
[01:35] Maya Ortega: totally understood. so first, SOC2 and ISO — redwood maintains SOC2 type II, and we also have an ISO-sum, i'll drop the certs. those are for our hosted environment; for Private we provide the control plane code and assist with compliance packaging.
[02:05] Ellen Morris: when you say "assist" what does that look like? do you hand over penetration test evidence or is that on the customer?
[02:20] Daniel Cho: good q. for Private deployments we do a shared-responsibility model — Redwood provides infrastructure hardening docs, audit log hooks, and process evidence. customer handles the host-level pen tests and any on-prem network configuration. for Hosted, we own the environment and we provide the SOC2 report and subservice organization info.
[02:50] Priya Singh: ok and for SAML — do you support SCIM for user provisioning? we want group-to-role mapping so our engineers get limited access.
[03:05] Maya Ortega: yes, we support SAML SSO + SCIM provisioning. RBAC roles are pluggable — standard roles in the console (admin, developer, viewer) and you can map identity groups to those. we'll also show how to restrict token scopes.
[03:34] Liam Navarro: is that the same for Dedicated? we want network isolation plus our own KMS.
[03:44] Daniel Cho: Dedicated adds VPC peering/private networking and more control — you can integrate your KMS via our KMS connector for BYOK in many clouds. for full BYOK with a local HSM you'd typically look at Private/on-prem where you fully control the key material.
[04:10] Asha Patel: any limitations on model telemetry or token logs with BYOK? we need to ensure we can still get per-request metadata for billing and debugging but without exposing raw payloads to the provider.
[04:30] Maya Ortega: good point — we separate telemetry (latency/cost tokens) from request payloads. in Hosted mode payloads are encrypted at rest with provider-managed keys, if BYOK is required we recommend Dedicated with KMS integration or Private to ensure the key never touches Redwood-managed keystores. we can redact or mask sensitive fields before storage if you need that.
[04:58] Priya Singh: when you say "redact" is that something we configure in the request pipeline? is there an SDK hook?
[05:12] Daniel Cho: yes, we have configurable pre-ingest transforms — you can plug in field-level masking rules. some customers do that in the client; others use a sidecar in their VPC for preprocessing in Private/Dedicated flows.
[05:38] Ellen Morris: audit logs — can logs be exported to our SIEM? we use Splunk and want push to our S3 bucket for archiving.
[05:52] Maya Ortega: absolutely — logs can stream to your S3 or to a SIEM via connectors. retention policy is configurable; Hosted default retention is 90 days for request-level, with export/long-term archive options. you can set up automated exports for 365+ retention.
[06:20] Liam Navarro: tamper evidence — what's the guarantee? do you use WORM storage or signed logs?
[06:36] Daniel Cho: we support signed log streams and you can enable immutable buckets for archive in your cloud tenant. Private gives the most guarantees since you control the archive. in Hosted we provide signed hashes and chain them so we can show tamper-evidence. note: the doc has details — i'll attach the log integrity flow.
[07:05] Asha Patel: good. data residency: we have EU customers and need EU-only processing for EU traffic. what's the mechanism?
[07:20] Maya Ortega: region routing is supported — you can pin requests to EU-hosted regions. Hosted can serve from region-specific clusters; Dedicated gives you reserved capacity in region; Private is fully in your region. we'll need to know which datasets must remain in EU.
[07:44] Priya Singh: encryption in transit? mTLS between client and Redwood?
[07:52] Daniel Cho: TLS 1.2/1.3 for all endpoints; for Dedicated you can enable mTLS and private endpoints inside your VPC. Private deployments typically use internal mTLS and can be locked down to internal networks.
[08:16] Ellen Morris: around SSO provisioning — can we limit who can call model-deploy APIs versus who can only call inference endpoints?
[08:30] Maya Ortega: yes, role-based controls: deployer role vs runtime role. you can issue scoped API keys with route-level permissions and short TTLs. we'll show token scoping in the console.
[08:55] Liam Navarro: ok can you walk me through the KMS options again — BYOK cloud provider KMS vs customer HSM — tradeoffs?
[09:08] Daniel Cho: sure. with cloud KMS BYOK, keys are in your cloud account and Redwood uses an integration to request decrypt/encrypt — Redwood doesn't store cleartext keys. HSM/BYOK where key material never leaves your HSM is possible with Private — Redwood calls your key via network HSM calls inside your VPC. tradeoff: Hosted with provider-managed keys is simplest but less control; Dedicated with cloud BYOK is middle ground; Private gives strongest control and increases operational overhead.
[09:50] Asha Patel: what's the overhead for Private? we have infosec budget but need to know the ops commitment.
[10:05] Maya Ortega: Private requires customer infra readiness — someone to manage updates, networking and KMS. Redwood offers an on-prem package and we support install/runbook & patches, but you'll need an infra owner. we also provide automation scripts to reduce daily ops.
[10:34] Priya Singh: about auditability — do you provide an immutable history of model version deployments and who rolled them out?
[10:45] Daniel Cho: yes, deployment audit trail is part of the console. every rollout, canary, or config change is recorded with user, timestamp, and diffs. you can export those records to your SIEM.
[11:12] Liam Navarro: any limitations on retention for per-token logs? we may want raw request logs for 180 days for debugging.
[11:25] Maya Ortega: Hosted default is 90 days; we can set up exports to extend. for 180 days we'd typically recommend automating export to your archive bucket or consider Dedicated with long-term retention configured. Private gives you full control.
[11:48] Asha Patel: compliance — for SOC2, do you provide an attestation letter or only the full report for customers after NDA?
[11:58] Maya Ortega: we provide a SOC2 type II report to customers under an NDA and also a summary/whitepaper publicly. i'll attach the formal report subject to NDA.
[12:12] Ellen Morris: do you do penetration testing on every release? customers often ask for pen-test cadence.
[12:22] Daniel Cho: we have a regular pen-test cadence — internal and third-party annually, and critical changes trigger targeted tests. for Private, customers usually run their own tests; we coordinate for high-risk changes.
[12:42] Priya Singh: operational question — if we provision Dedicated, can we burst to more GPUs or is it fixed?
[12:55] Maya Ortega: Dedicated supports autoscaling and burst policies, you can reserve baseline nodes and allow burst capacity; there are config knobs for autoscale thresholds. performance and latency SLOs are provided in the contract.
[13:18] Liam Navarro: about the console's token-level breakdown you mentioned earlier — will that leak content in logs?
[13:30] Daniel Cho: token-level cost breakdown is metadata only — token counts and latency, not raw user content. raw content is only retained in request logs which are encrypted and subject to your retention policy. we can also redact or not store request bodies for higher privacy.
[13:55] Asha Patel: do you support HIPAA BAA? we have some PHI flows in the future plan.
[14:05] Maya Ortega: Redwood can support HIPAA customers; we'd stand up a BAA as part of the enterprise onboarding. some deployment modes (Private/ Dedicated with certain controls) are recommended.
[14:22] Priya Singh: any story on RBAC for service accounts used by our workers? can we rotate keys automatically?
[14:34] Daniel Cho: service accounts support short-lived tokens via our token service and you can integrate with your identity provider for automated rotation. we also support key rotation policies in KMS.
[14:56] Ellen Morris: question on legal/audit — can logs be delivered in a forensically sound format for audits?
[15:08] Maya Ortega: yes, we can produce exports with signed checksums and chain of custody notes; that's part of our enterprise compliance kit.
[15:28] Asha Patel: timeline for pilot — we want to run a pilot for 6 weeks, start with small Dedicated pool, run throughput tests and security review. what's typical runway?
[15:40] Maya Ortega: typical pilot is 4–6 weeks. first week is setup and connectivity (SAML, KMS test), following weeks are benchmarks and security verification. we'll need your infra contact and legal to sign the NDA for SOC2 docs.
[16:02] Priya Singh: do you have a standard benchmark harness? we want reproducible numbers — batch sizes, sequence lengths, p99 latency.
[16:15] Daniel Cho: yes, we'll provide a benchmark harness and a spreadsheet template. we'll run a baseline against a 3-node dedicated pool and share the results.
[16:36] Liam Navarro: curious — do any customers combine Redwood Hosted endpoints for low-sensitivity traffic and Private for high sensitivity?
[16:48] Maya Ortega: yep, hybrid routing is common — route low-sensitivity calls to Hosted for cost savings and route PHI or regulated traffic into Dedicated/Private. Smart routing policies can be based on headers or tenant id.
[17:10] Priya Singh: are there infra checklist items we should prepare before the pilot?
[17:18] Daniel Cho: yes — we'll send a connectivity checklist (VPC CIDR, allowed egress, KMS roles, SAML metadata, SIEM endpoints).
[17:34] Ellen Morris: one last detail — retention policy enforcement: if we auto-export logs to our S3 with lifecycle rules, can Redwood delete hosted copies to ensure single authoritative copy?
[17:48] Maya Ortega: yes, we can configure auto-delete after export; we'll coordinate retention in the contract.
[18:05] Asha Patel: ok thanks — feels like the major concerns covered. next steps?
[18:12] Maya Ortega: action items: i'll send SOC2/ISO docs under NDA, daniel will send benchmark plan; we'll propose times for a Dedicated walkthrough and get Priya's throughput matrix.
[18:28] Priya Singh: i'll share our throughput matrix by Monday.
[18:34] Daniel Cho: noted. one technical note — if you decide on BYOK cloud KMS, we'll need a dedicated KMS role in your cloud account to grant decrypt for Redwood connector. we'll include specifics in the checklist.
[18:56] Liam Navarro: ok, I'm also going to look at data residency for EU and will send a short doc on which datasets must remain EU.
[19:08] Maya Ortega: perfect. we'll follow up with a calendar invite for the Dedicated walkthrough and the NDA link to access SOC2.
[19:20] Asha Patel: thanks everyone.
[19:24] [meeting ends]

Notes/Artifacts referenced:
- Redwood SOC2 Type II (attachment link — NDA required)
- ISO summary whitepaper (public link)
- KMS integration diagram (will be attached by Daniel)
- Benchmark spreadsheet template (will be shared)

Recorded duration roughly 41 minutes. Some transcription errors expected (product names sometimes misheard, e.g., "k-v cash" instead of KV cache, "Redwood dedicate" for Dedicated).
